title: Mekkablood, a game I made with a custom gpt using DALL-E 3
author: Mekkablood

comments.author: DreamNotDeferred
comments.body: Looks cool. What was your work pipeline?

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body: Thanks, I use the gpt I made (16-bit multiview is the name) which helps make the sprites in multiple angles(works about half the time). Then throw it in photoshop and put my own spin on it/clean them up. Toss everything in Ue5, shake everything up then bam you have a video game.

replies.author: MrMiichou
replies.body: How long all the process took you ?

replies.author: MrMiichou
replies.body: Wow pretty impressive ! Again, nice job !

replies.author: gglang_mtl
replies.body: Rad. How did you make the animations? Looks like there are some sprite sheets involved in some places?

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body: Just used photoshop for each frame.

replies.author: DreamNotDeferred
replies.body:
Thanks for replying. Maybe willing to give a brief description of what it means to make a gpt? Are you talking about training a model, or something more elaborate? 

Also, you mentioned that you didn't know much coding and got a lot of use out of the AI in that area, how were your unreal skills when you started? Did AI do any part of that as well?

Thanks again

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body:
Openai lets you make gpt's which are presets of instruction before your prompt. You can use it too it's called 16-bit multiview but probobly requires a chatgpt+ subscription. 

I did not mention that I got a lot of use of ai for coding in fact I used none. I did have experience with Ue5 prior to this but was by no means a pro at it. Best to find a paid course for the game type you want and make sure it tells you how to do saves and a menu properly.

replies.author: DreamNotDeferred
replies.body: Ah sorry, may have been confusing your post with another, for the coding part. In any case, very impressive work, thanks for sharing.

comments.author: WillowKisz
comments.body: damn it looks like those of arcade video games. It looks ridiculously good!!!! Can you please guide us on the process or point us to some guide to achieve that? Thank you good sir

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body: You can try the gpt I mentioned in the other comment if you have a chatgpt+ subscription(might work for free users, not sure). Then type in whatever object or character type you want for the art and reminding chat gpt to follow the gpt's directions at times(especially to start off). Definitely want to have some photoshop skills already to go along with this. From there It's just knowing how to use UE5, which I would recommend going with a paid course that's well reviewed for the game type you want to do.

replies.author: WillowKisz
replies.body:
The problem I had in the past with paid chatgpt is that, it has limits. I think no more than 40 requests or lower? So I opted for ComfyUI and Stable Diffusion. 

I got it. Thanks for the input!

replies.author: SalamanderOk6944
replies.body: How long does it take to generate the output?  It's told me to stay tuned!

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body: Maybe openai is having issues, it usually takes me about 5-10 seconds. On the first prompt you gotta tell it to follow the gpt's directions.

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body: working fine for me, do you have a chatgpt+ subscription? The name is 16-bit multiview.

comments.author: _stevencasteel_
comments.body: Agreed, this looks really great! Sounds like you are using Suno for the music? [Udio](https://youtu.be/FF4mtbW8Ros?si=0QJq6LG7NTUUbUZL) is many magnitudes less artifacty / low bitrate sounding.

comments.author: Fluid_Cup8329
comments.body: Fantastic work! Did you use ai to help out with any programming, or just for the art?

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body: Thanks, just the art. I don't think any ai does blueprint well yet, but I could be wrong.

replies.author: Fluid_Cup8329
replies.body: I've had gpt help me marginally with blueprints in the past, but mostly unsuccessful because of how frequently things can change in UE, or inaccuracies in the ai.
